# crosswork_metric_thresholds (Resource)

This resource can manage the metric thresholds of the topology.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "crosswork_metric_thresholds" "example" {
  thresholds = {
    "Utilization" = {
      levels = [
        {
          severity    = "CRITICAL"
          upper_value = 100
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `thresholds` (Attributes Map) Thresholds by metric, `Utilization`, `Errors`, `Drops`, `Delay`, `Jitter`, `Loss` or `Power`. A metric that is not listed keeps its thresholds (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--thresholds))

### Optional

- `instance` (String) Select an instance of the provider configuration by its name. Leave it unset to use the default instance.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The id of the object

<a id="nestedatt--thresholds"></a>
### Nested Schema for `thresholds`

Required:

- `levels` (Attributes List) Levels of the metric, from the lowest value up. The last level of a percentage metric ends at 100 and the last level of `Delay` and `Jitter` is `CRITICAL` with -1; the controller drops any other `CRITICAL` row (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--thresholds--levels))

<a id="nestedatt--thresholds--levels"></a>
### Nested Schema for `thresholds.levels`

Required:

- `severity` (String) Severity of the level
  - Choices: `HEALTHY`, `MINOR`, `MAJOR`, `CRITICAL`
- `upper_value` (Number) Upper value of the level. Percentages are 0 to 100, `Delay` and `Jitter` are in microseconds

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import crosswork_metric_thresholds.example "metric_thresholds"
```
